mathematical_review.model_and_quantifiers: An undirected cactus whose blocks are single edges or single cycles, with a positive integer weight w(e) charged equally at either endpoint. A chosen direction u→v charges w(e) to its tail u. The threshold engine permits nonnegative node loads f(v), including zero, and asks whether f(v)+sum_outgoing w(e)≤K for every vertex. Node loads record already fixed outgoing original edges. The registered optimization guarantee is only the original zero-initial-load {1,…,k}-MMO domain. No machine-dependent endpoint times, arbitrary eligibility, configuration coupling, prescribed row laws or general unrelated-machine algorithm is obtained.
mathematical_review.invariant: After a block reduction, a remaining vertex has its original f plus exactly the total weights of fixed original edges directed out of it. Each removed vertex has every incident direction fixed and final load≤K. A K-feasible orientation exists before the step iff one exists in the resulting residual instance; recorded directions extend any residual witness. This invariant proves actual feasibility and recovery, rather than merely monotonicity of a scalar bound.
mathematical_review.cycle_rule_2_1a: For a non-gate u with f(u)+w(e)+w(e′)≤K, direct both cycle edges away from u and delete u. From any original feasible orientation, reversing any of these two edges into outgoing edges at u only decreases the neighbors’ charges; u remains within K by the displayed inequality. Conversely any residual feasible orientation extends by these two arcs with u feasible. The non-gate restriction ensures there are no unaccounted external edges at u.
mathematical_review.cycle_rule_2_1b: If f(u)+w({u,v})>K, u cannot pay that edge in any feasible solution. It must be directed v→u. Removing it and increasing f(v) by w(e) is an exact residual equivalence, not just a one-way necessary condition. If the increase exceeds K, infeasibility is justified immediately.
mathematical_review.cycle_rule_2_1c_complete_proof: When neither earlier cycle rule applies, every non-gate u satisfies f(u)+w(e_u)+w(e′_u)>K, while every endpoint can pay either individual incident cycle edge. Thus every non-gate has at most one outgoing cycle edge in a feasible orientation. A cycle with r edges needs r outgoing edge tails in total; if its unique gate g paid zero cycle edges, the other r−1 vertices could supply at most r−1 tails, impossible. Consequently any feasible cycle orientation makes g pay at least min{w(e_g),w(e′_g)}. Direct the entire cycle consistently so g pays precisely that lighter edge. Every non-gate pays exactly one edge and is feasible by failure of 2-1b. The gate contribution is no larger than in any original feasible solution, so all fixed outside-block directions can be retained. This gives the minimum possible residual gate burden, hence full feasibility preservation. If there is no gate, any consistently directed cycle is feasible by the same individual-edge inequalities. With e_g={g,x}, e′_g={g,y}, w(e_g)≥w(e′_g), frozen Fig.3 uses x→g and g→y, adds w(e_g) to f(x), adds w(e′_g) to f(g). The gate pays the lighter edge. The former heavier-gate wording would have broken this minimal-interface proof; the current correction agrees with the actual frozen algorithm and does not weaken the theorem.
mathematical_review.path_rule: Peel a leaf of the current block while treating its surviving gate as the exterior interface. If f(u)+w(e)≤K, choosing u→v discharges u and leaves the neighbor with the least possible new burden; reorienting a feasible v→u in this way cannot harm v. Otherwise v→u is forced and its exact charge is added to f(v). Repeating preserves the invariant. An isolated remainder is accepted exactly when its accumulated load≤K.
mathematical_review.upper_bound_and_search: A constructive bound is OPT≤f_max+2w_max: in each leaf cycle choose a non-gate u and direct both edges out of it, then peel the remaining paths toward the surviving interface; for K=f_max+2w_max every such choice and every leaf one-edge payment fits, and no remaining node load is increased. For zero initial loads and at least one edge, w_max≤OPT≤2w_max. Binary search this integer interval, using the decision witness at the final feasible threshold, gives O(log(w_max+1)) calls and therefore O(n log(k+1)) arithmetic/comparison operations when w_max≤k. For k≥2 this is the published O(n log k); k=1 and edgeless inputs are handled directly in O(n). If k is merely an allowed upper bound rather than an attained edge weight, OPT≥k is not valid, but using w_max fixes the interval without changing the advertised asymptotics. The current body does not rely on the incorrect lower bound k.
mathematical_review.recovery_scope: The algorithm fixes original edge directions during reduction; store an edge-ID→direction record (or a stack including both 2-1a arcs and the two 2-1c arcs). Each original edge is recorded exactly once, so a successful run recovers one complete K-feasible original orientation in O(n) additional operations and O(n) records. During block deletion, the surviving cut vertex remains as the external interface with its accumulated load; removing its block-local occurrence does not delete its other incident blocks. The optimization reruns the decision algorithm from the original input at the final feasible K if a witness was not retained. Tail assignment then returns exactly the equal-time two-endpoint restricted schedule. It does not recover a witness for arbitrary endpoint-dependent times or for unrelated configuration/row-law problems.
mathematical_review.frozen_proof_precision: The printed Lemma6 component symbols in the 2-1c paragraph and compressed pseudo-code bookkeeping should be read through the explicit minimal-gate exchange above. This review does not rely on its component inequality as a standalone proof, and does not relabel this already resolved precision point as a new mathematical open obligation.

complexity_and_encoding.arithmetic_model: For n vertices and m=O(n) edges, constructing the block forest, maintaining its leaves, scanning each cycle for the first applicable case and peeling its path examine each vertex/edge only O(1) times. With adjacency lists and a queue there is no repeated whole-graph search. Each fixed arc, load addition and threshold comparison is constant time in the paper’s integer-arithmetic/word model, giving O(n) threshold decisions and O(n) orientation output operations.
complexity_and_encoding.binary_threshold_cost: For binary input, let B=ceil(log2(2+K+f_max+m w_max)) for nonnegative K (negative thresholds reject immediately). Each residual load is an initial load plus some original incident weights, so this bounds every numeric value. Ordinary addition/comparison costs O(B) bit operations, hence O(nB) for the numeric part of one decision, in addition to reading the actual input and graph-index/storage costs. The O(n) theorem must not be described as O(n) bit operations for arbitrarily long integer encodings.
complexity_and_encoding.binary_optimization_cost: In the zero-load optimization search K≤2w_max≤2k. Abort immediately after any update exceeds K (or saturate at K+1), so all numeric intermediates have O(log(k+1)) bits. There are O(n log(k+1)) numeric operations across the search. A safe ordinary-bit-arithmetic bound for that numeric part is O(n log²(k+1)), plus the actual input and graph-index costs. On a word-RAM whose word holds vertex indices and these weights/loads, the published O(n log(k+1)) operation bound applies. No unary assumption, pseudo-polynomial dependence on k, or uncharged arbitrary-precision arithmetic is being introduced.
complexity_and_encoding.space_and_output: O(n) edge/orientation records and current graph records suffice; numeric storage is O(nB) bits for a threshold run. Writing the n-scale direction witness and reading all input integers remain necessary. k=1 and empty-edge cases do not have zero time merely because log k=0.
complexity_and_encoding.no_new_algorithm_claim: These encoding qualifications explain the existing theorem’s model. This review does not claim a new strongly linear bit algorithm, a linear-time optimization breakthrough, or a new block-rank-to-cactus comparison theorem.
